text: I want emotional closeness, but I feel unsafe when someone gets close.
I feel disloyal to this caregiver when I make choices they would not want.
I feel that something is wrong with me as a person.
I feel responsible for other people’s distress even when I did not cause it.
I keep returning in my thoughts to relationships that have ended.
I handle emotional difficulties alone rather than let someone know I need support.
I put off changes because I do not want to lose what is familiar.
I fear that people would reject me if they knew me well.
I feel responsible for protecting this caregiver from loneliness.
I keep important feelings to myself even when someone invites me to share them.
I stay alert for signs that someone close to me might turn against me.
I feel guilty when I say no to a request that I cannot reasonably meet.
I hold on to a relationship that no longer works for me because ending it feels too painful.
I pull away after a moment of emotional closeness because I feel exposed to harm.
I put this caregiver’s emotional needs ahead of the adult life I want.
I feel ashamed of needing emotional support.
I present myself as needing very little from other people.
I put aside my own needs because expressing them feels like burdening others.
I struggle to accept that an important period of my life is over.
I feel I should be this caregiver’s main source of emotional support.
I take criticism of something I did as a judgment of my worth as a person.
I find it hard to trust that someone will keep treating me kindly.
I feel guilty about doing well when someone close to me is struggling.
I expect my emotional needs to go unnoticed.
I try to hide parts of myself that I believe are unacceptable.
I find it hard to ask for help even when help is available.
I limit closeness with other people to protect my special bond with this caregiver.
I feel threatened by disagreements with someone close to me.
I help people mainly to reduce my guilt about not helping.
I keep possessions mainly because letting them go feels like losing part of my past.
I find it hard to invest in a new relationship while missing an old one.
I feel an urge to escape when someone is tender toward me.
I defend myself quickly when I feel someone has exposed a personal flaw.
I feel unknown by people who spend a lot of time with me.
I blame myself for problems that are outside my control.
I need this caregiver’s approval before I feel free to make a major life choice.
I feel safer with some emotional distance, even when I want more connection.
I make room for other people’s feelings while keeping my own out of view.
I put someone else down when comparing myself with them makes me feel inferior.
I feel preoccupied with the possibility of losing people who matter to me.
I hold back from asserting myself because I fear hurting someone.
I feel guilty about setting limits on this caregiver’s access to me.
I choose a familiar but unsatisfying situation because moving on feels too painful.
I hold back from becoming more independent because it feels like abandoning this caregiver.
I shut down emotionally when closeness feels overwhelming.
I feel uncomfortable letting someone take care of me.
I feel that enjoying myself is wrong when someone else needs support.
I rely on being close to someone I admire to feel worthwhile myself.
